The act of state doctrine means a domestic court will not judge the validity of a foreign government's official acts carried out within that government's own territory, even if they allegedly breach international law. The note's premise is inverted: the doctrine rests on separation of powers and the view that courts are ill-suited to assess foreign state conduct, not on judges' expertise to do so. Exceptions and scope vary by jurisdiction; in the US, *Banco Nacional de Cuba v. Sabbatino* is the leading case.
